sense.text:
“Wherefore the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men.” The precept of men is the doctrine of men.

The Trinity is exactly that. The doctrine of trinitarianism is a doctrine and commandment of men, and this whole class is to show it. It was taught ten years ago in the first part; this is the second part, revisited, because it is ridiculous. It is madness, borderline insanity, a doctrine for people who are on the spectrum, people who are not in their right mind. Some of you came out of the Catholic Church and have some knowledge of it; some do not. Either way, it is the fear of God taught by the precept of men.

precepts.why:
Christ says the same thing: “Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.”

You had the elders in Isaiah’s day teaching the doctrines of men, and then the Pharisees in Christ’s time doing the exact same thing, because those elders had children, and those children became the opposition of Christ in his time.

“Teaching for doctrines the commandments of men”: that is exactly what the Trinity is.

sense.text: “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments.” A good understanding comes to those that do the commandments. That is the foundation of understanding: doing the commandments and fearing God. It is an action, and the doing is what grants you understanding.

precepts.why:
When you have that understanding: “All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing froward or perverse in them. They are all plain to him that understandeth.” And you understand how? By fearing God and keeping his commandments. That is where the understanding comes from. The words of God are plain to him or her that keeps the laws of God: plain, clear, no deepness, no confusion.

“And right to them that find knowledge”: the knowledge that is right is what is found in the Bible. Step outside the Bible and the word of God is not right to you.

“A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not.” The wisdom the scorner seeks is wisdom outside the Bible, the doctrines of men. That is the scorner, because they hate the Bible, they hate the scriptures, they hate the laws, so they go seeking wisdom elsewhere: Egyptology, Christianity, Islam. And they find it not.

“But knowledge is easy unto him that understandeth”: the knowledge of God is easy to him that understands, that keeps the commandments. It goes back to understanding.

“As his ways are plain unto the holy; so are they stumblingblocks unto the wicked.” The Bible is very clear. It is self-defining and self-explanatory, and it does not require any outside source to explain it: not a so-called church father of the second, third or fourth century, not a catechism, a curriculum, a theology or a christology. The Bible explains itself, and it is plain to them that keep his laws and commandments.

It is a stumblingblock to the wicked because they are doing everything the Bible says not to do. They argue whether Christ is the Most High, whether the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are all one, all deep, dark, metaphorical stuff, while they celebrate Christmas, New Year’s, Halloween, Carnival, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Valentine’s and birthdays. They want to argue Bible while doing things not found in the Bible. That is hypocrisy. Let’s argue his essence and his substance: what is the essence of Christmas? What is the substance of New Year’s or Halloween? There is none.

It is all a smoke screen to do what God says not to do. It is an intellectual measuring contest, I’m smarter than you, and most of the time there is money at the end of it. And the nation mostly behind these Trinitarian and Unitarian arguments is Edom. Esau is the main culprit, because the so-called white man gained power over the Catholic Church, whitewashed everything and spread this ideology.

“For wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit”. In wisdom is an understanding spirit, “holy, one only, manifold, subtil, lively, clear, undefiled, plain”. Wisdom is clear. Proverbs said the words of God are plain, and here wisdom is clear and plain: when you are keeping God’s commandments, the word of God becomes plain and clear.

“Not subject to hurt”: it can’t be damaged. “Which cannot be letted”: it can’t be stopped. “Ready to do good, Kind to man, steadfast, sure”. The Bible is sure. The laws of God are sure, the prophecies of God are sure, us being God’s people is sure, Christ being the Messiah is sure, there being a God is sure.

“Free from care” means free from worry. “Having all power, overseeing all things, and going through all understanding, pure, and most subtil, spirits”: there are deep things behind it, and there are spirits in this book.

sense.text: Remember the scorner seeks wisdom and finds it not. Here is the wisdom he finds: “This wisdom descendeth not from above”. It is not of God. “But is earthly”, of man; “sensual”, emotional; “devilish”, evil, satanic. That is where the confusion of these debates comes from.

sense.text:

“Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech”. That hope is faith, and that faith is in Christ. When we have faith and hope in Christ we use great plainness of speech, because, remember, wisdom is plain and clear.

precepts.why:

That is why we don’t sit down with that apologist who stalks us and mocks us, with the Bible open in front of him while he gets paid at our expense. That book doesn’t even belong to him; it shouldn’t even be in his hand.

“Let mine adversaries be clothed with shame, and let them cover themselves with their own confusion, as with a mantle.” That is what this is. The adversaries of God and his people cover themselves with their own confusion. “As with a mantle”: they wear their confusion.

sense.text:

precepts.why:

There is no all-inclusive church; it doesn’t say he was in the Catholic church. The church in the wilderness is the church the Bible deals with, God’s congregation, the one the prophets are sent to, and no one else outside of that.

“And with our fathers: who received the lively oracles to give unto us”. Those are the fathers of the church: the elders who received the laws of God.

The old dictionary of 1849 says it too: the apostles supported their doctrine entirely by evidence and needed no human laws or worldly policy, but once they were dead the whole Christian system underwent a miserable change. Those are the church fathers: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Isaiah, Daniel, Paul, Peter, John, Mark, Luke, and most likely Polycarp, who kept the orthodox doctrine, though he is not named in the Bible. The Catholic in the video speaks of one essence, distinct in personhood, with the sign of the cross and two fingers for Christ fully God and fully man, and he uses no Bible. The one scripture he quoted is this: “I and my Father are one.”

But if the Father has the divine essence and is God, and the Son has the divine essence and is God, and Christ kept both humanity and Godhood on the earth, then he is his own God. Not only is he his own God, he has two Gods: himself, and the God above him. It is a ridiculous argument.

In the debate the Trinitarian admitted there is an element of philosophy in it. It is not an element; it is full-blown philosophy. Nowhere in Psalms 22 do we read that Christ, out of his mother’s womb, is fully God and fully man. That is a Greco-Roman hermeneutical interpretation, not scripture.

precepts.why: “Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?” He is the God of all flesh. So if Christ is the essence of his Father, then Christ is the God over his own flesh, his own God over his own humanity. That is exactly what the Trinitarian said in the debate, and even his own side laughed, because they know it is stupid. That question alone stumped them, but they kept going. It is a cartwheel; these are unreasonable people who will not yield to reason.

sense.text: “Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God”: that is one. “And I will write upon him the name of my God”: two. “And the name of the city of my God”: three. “Which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God”: four. Christ, resurrected and glorified, says “my God” four times in one verse. The Bible is clear and concise.

precepts.why:
After Christ resurrected: “Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father”. Unto who? My Father. Not myself. “I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.” My God, your God, my Father, your Father, because he is the grandfather of us all. That is 1 Corinthians 8:6: clear and concise.

There is no scripture in the Bible that shows the heavenly Father becomes Christ’s God only when he is a human being, as opposed to being his God always. That is pure theology. Ask them where the Bible says it.

sense.text: The Bible does say that God is the God of Christ even when Christ is in the form of God. “Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God”. Even in the form of God, Christ reckoned that God is God. Whether a man or a God, he knows the Father is above him.

Verse 6 ends with a colon, so verse 7 explains it. “But made himself of no reputation”: that goes back to not robbery to be equal with God. “And took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men”. In the Greek, “made himself of no reputation” is said to mean he emptied himself. Not like a tea kettle: it means he humbled himself and took on the status of a servant, even though he was a king and the son of God on the earth. He made himself void of the title of being above everybody else. That is why he washed their feet.

Verse 7 ends with a colon too, so verse 8 explains it. “And being found in fashion as a man”: back to the likeness of men, made like everybody else, of mother and father. “He humbled himself”: back to the form of a servant and no reputation, the same thing. “And became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.”

“Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name”. If they are the same, what name could he possibly be given that is higher? It makes no sense. “That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow”, “And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.” A distinction: God exalted him, to the glory of God the Father.

At the end of the day, this is what it comes down to, in the Hellenistic period and now. “Not setting by the honours of their fathers”: they did not care for the honour of their fathers, their forefathers in the scriptures, the Bible. “But liking the glory of the Grecians best of all”: the philosophy and glory of the Greeks. That goes for the Council of Nicaea too, and for these panels today.

“By reason whereof sore calamity came upon them”: destruction and captivity. “For they had them to be their enemies and avengers, whose custom they followed so earnestly”: their custom, their philosophy, dress, language, traditions and education. We do it now in Christianity with this Trinitarian doctrine: we follow the customs of the Greeks earnestly. “And unto whom they desired to be like in all things.” That is why they sit among us in these debates: because we desire to be like them in all things.
